fatal_errors: The proposed material is an unspecified refractory HEA rather than the FeNiCrCoCu FCC HEA coating used on the Cu matrix.
No cited evidence establishes that a refractory HEA adheres effectively to Cu or is structurally compatible with the Cu substrate.
The oxidation-film mechanism is unrelated to the target temperature-dependent lattice disorder, dislocation evolution, hardness, and friction mechanism.
The claimed 800–1200 °C boundary conflicts with the target 900 K threshold and is not supported as a Cu-coating wear boundary.
The evidence only supports generic properties of bulk refractory HEAs; it does not support the proposed Cu-matrix coating intervention or its wear performance.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly recognizes that an HEA coating might improve surface protection, but it fails to identify the target FeNiCrCoCu coating and reconstructs neither the nanoindentation/friction intervention nor its temperature dependence. Its dense-oxide-film explanation applies only to suitably alloyed RHEAs containing elements such as Al, Cr, or Si and does not establish adhesion to Cu. The predicted improvement also misses the observed sharp deterioration in hardness and wear resistance at and above 900 K. Although the proposed coated-versus-uncoated comparison is falsifiable, it is generic and would not discriminate the target mechanism without temperature-resolved measurements of lattice order, HCP fraction, dislocation density, modulus, hardness, and friction.
